observations: Photo 0: Front view of an iPhone with a visible notch, displaying iOS home screen with app icons. The screen appears to be on and functional.
Photo 1: Back view of the phone showing a gold-colored glass back with severe spiderweb cracks radiating from the camera module. The camera lenses are protected by decorative rings.
Photo 2: Side and front view with screen off, showing a black front with visible smudges and a small crack or chip at the bottom edge of the screen.
No visible branding or model text on any photo. The seller claims it is an iPhone 11 Pro Max 512GB.

claims.evidence: The phone's design (notch, triple rear camera layout) is consistent with an iPhone 11 Pro Max, but no model or storage label is visible in any photo. The seller's text is not proof.
No photo shows the battery or any service record. The claim cannot be verified from the images.

risks.risk: Severe back glass damage may affect structural integrity and water resistance.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the back glass showing the extent of cracks and whether the camera module is damaged or loose.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as having major cosmetic damage and potential functional risk.

risks.risk: Front screen may have hidden damage or dead pixels not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video showing the screen being touched and swiped across all areas, including the bottom edge where a crack is visible.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as having possible screen damage, reducing value.

risks.risk: Battery replacement may be poor quality or not genuine, affecting performance and safety.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the battery health percentage from Settings > Battery > Battery Health, or a video showing the battery being tested under load.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as having unverified battery condition, assuming worst-case performance.

risks.risk: Device may be stolen, blacklisted, or have iCloud lock.
risks.proof: A video showing the phone being turned on, with the seller entering their Apple ID and password, and then showing the 'Find My' status as 'This iPhone is not lost'.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially locked or blacklisted, which would render it unusable for the buyer.

proof_requests: Video showing the phone being turned on, with the seller logging into their Apple ID and showing 'Find My' status as 'This iPhone is not lost'.
Close-up photo of the back glass showing the full extent of cracks and camera module condition.
Video of the screen being swiped and touched across all areas, especially the bottom edge.
Screenshot of battery health from Settings > Battery > Battery Health.
response.reason: The phone's identity is consistent with an iPhone 11 Pro Max but cannot be confirmed without visible model text. The back glass is severely cracked, and the front screen may have damage. Battery and iCloud status are unverified. These hidden risks require proof before pricing can be determined.
